Definition: Readiness of IT infrastructure, platforms, and DR site capabilities to support system recovery during a disaster.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No dedicated DR infrastructure, recovery depends on rebuilding systems manually on available resources.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic DR setup exists (e.g. backups or limited standby systems), but capacity and readiness are not sufficient for full recovery.
Level 3 - Defined: DR environment is established for critical systems, infrastructure and replication are configured but not fully validated.
Level 4 - Managed: DR infrastructure is sized and maintained to support critical workloads, replication and failover capabilities are regularly tested.
Level 5 - Optimized: DR infrastructure is robust and scalable, systems can be recovered reliably across sites with minimal disruption.

Definition: Maximum acceptable time to restore a system or application after a disruption
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: RTO is not defined, recovery timelines are unpredictable and depend on manual effort.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic RTO targets exist for a few critical systems, but are not consistently achieved.
Level 3 - Defined: RTO is defined per application, recovery procedures are documented but execution varies.
Level 4 - Managed: RTO targets are consistently met for critical systems through tested DR processes.
Level 5 - Optimized: Recovery is streamlined with automated failover, RTO is minimized and consistently achieved across workloads.

Definition: Maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: RPO is not defined, data loss during failure is unpredictable.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic RPO targets exist for a few critical systems, but backups are infrequent and inconsistent.
Level 3 - Defined: RPO is defined per application, backup/replication schedules are aligned but not always met.
Level 4 - Managed: RPO targets are consistently achieved using regular backups or replication for critical systems.
Level 5 - Optimized: Near real-time data protection for critical workloads, minimal data loss with continuous or frequent replication.

Definition: Availability and accessibility of backup data during a disaster for successful recovery.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Backups may exist but are not readily accessible during a disaster, recovery is uncertain.
Level 2 - Developing: Backups are available for some critical systems but may require manual effort or delays to access.
Level 3 - Defined: Backups are available for most critical workloads and can be accessed within defined procedures.
Level 4 - Managed: Backup data is consistently available and accessible within defined RTO/RPO requirements, including offsite storage.
Level 5 - Optimized: Backup data is readily accessible across locations (e.g. DR site/cloud) with minimal delay, supporting reliable recovery for most workloads.

Definition: Ability to switch operations to a DR environment (failover) and return to primary site (failback) with minimal disruption.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No defined failover or failback process, recovery is manual and unstructured.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic failover possible for a few systems, but largely manual, failback process is unclear or untested.
Level 3 - Defined: Failover and failback procedures are documented, partial execution possible but requires manual coordination.
Level 4 - Managed: Failover and failback are tested and can be executed within defined RTO, processes are standardized for critical systems.
Level 5 - Optimized: Failover and failback are streamlined with minimal manual effort, regularly tested and reliable across critical workloads.

Definition: Availability, accuracy, and usability of documented DR plans, procedures, and dependencies.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No formal DR documentation, recovery depends on individual knowledge.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic DR documents exist for some systems, but are incomplete, outdated, or not easily accessible.
Level 3 - Defined: DR procedures are documented for critical systems, documents are available but not regularly updated.
Level 4 - Managed: Comprehensive DR documentation is maintained, regularly updated, and aligned with current infrastructure and processes.
Level 5 - Optimized: DR documentation is standardized, version-controlled, easily accessible, and validated through regular DR testing and audits.

Definition: Identification, assessment, and mitigation of risks that could impact business continuity.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No formal risk assessment, risks are addressed only after incidents occur.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic risk identification performed for some areas, assessments are informal and not regularly updated.
Level 3 - Defined: Structured risk assessment process exists, key risks are documented and periodically reviewed.
Level 4 - Managed: Comprehensive risk assessments are conducted regularly, mitigation plans are defined and tracked.
Level 5 - Optimized: Risk management is integrated into business processes with continuous monitoring and regular updates aligned to business changes.

Definition: Process of identifying critical business functions, dependencies, and the impact of disruptions (including RTO/RPO requirements).
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No formal BIA performed, critical business functions and impacts are not clearly understood.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic BIA conducted for a few critical functions, lacks consistency and is not regularly updated.
Level 3 - Defined: Structured BIA completed for key business units, critical functions, dependencies, and RTO/RPO are documented.
Level 4 - Managed: Comprehensive BIA covering all major business functions, reviewed periodically and aligned with business priorities.
Level 5 - Optimized: BIA is regularly updated and integrated into planning, used to drive DR/BC strategies and investment decisions.

Definition: Defined processes for internal and external communication during a disruption, including roles, escalation paths, and stakeholders.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No formal communication plan, coordination happens informally during incidents.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic contact lists exist, but roles, escalation paths, and communication methods are unclear.
Level 3 - Defined: Communication plan is documented with defined roles, contact lists, and escalation procedures.
Level 4 - Managed: Communication plans are regularly updated, tested during drills, and include internal and external stakeholders.
Level 5 - Optimized: Communication is well-coordinated and timely during incidents, plans are integrated with crisis management and continuously improved.

Definition: Defined approaches to maintain or quickly resume critical business operations during disruptions (e.g. alternate sites, remote work, manual workarounds, DR alignment).
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No defined continuity strategies, business relies on reactive decisions during disruptions.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic strategies exist for a few critical functions (e.g. manual workarounds), but are not formalized or consistent.
Level 3 - Defined: Continuity strategies are documented for key business functions, aligned with BIA, but not fully tested.
Level 4 - Managed: Strategies are implemented, tested, and aligned with DR capabilities, alternate arrangements (sites, resources) are in place.
Level 5 - Optimized: Continuity strategies are regularly validated, adaptable to different scenarios, and integrated into overall business operations.

Definition: Readiness of personnel, roles, responsibilities, and operational processes to support business continuity during disruptions.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No defined roles or processes, response depends on individual effort and availability.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic roles are identified for key personnel, but responsibilities and processes are unclear or inconsistent.
Level 3 - Defined: Roles and responsibilities are documented, continuity processes are defined but not consistently practiced.
Level 4 - Managed: Teams are trained on their roles, processes are tested through drills and followed during incidents.
Level 5 - Optimized: Roles and processes are well understood across teams, regular training and improvements ensure consistent and effective response
